item.content: {"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=theoretical+models+of+value+divergence+in+multi-agent+reinforcement+learning+identical+initial+conditions&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.31390/gradschool_theses.6213\", \"title\": [\"ADAPTIVE MULTI-AGENT REINFORCEMENT LEARNING FOR ELECTRIC VEHICLE CHARGING OPTIMIZATION UNDER DYNAMIC TRAFFIC CONDITIONS\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.31390/gradschool_theses.6213\"}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1016/j.ejcon.2025.101354\", \"title\": [\"Robust iterative learning control of continuous delayed singular multi-agent systems with polytopic uncertainty and non-identical initial conditions: LMI approach\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejcon.2025.101354\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2025, 9]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.6682038\", \"title\": [\"Multi-Agent Large Language Models with Reinforcement Learning for Quant Trading\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>The growing complexity and non-stationarity of financial markets make it increasingly difficult for traditional quantitative models to design robust trading strategies. Manually constructed alpha signals tend to exhibit limited adaptability when market conditions change, while machine learning-based approaches frequently lack interpretability and generalization across assets. To solve these issues, this research explores an alternative approach in which large language models (LLMs) are incorporated into the alpha design and portfolio weighting process. Specifically, we introduce a novel framework that integrates a multi-agent LLM system with reinforcement learning to improve formulaic alpha generation and portfolio allocation. In our setup, DeepSeek serves as the generation agent to construct a diverse pool of formulaic alphas, while Gemini acts as the evaluation agent to filter and select the most promising candidates. The selected alphas are then incorporated into a Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) framework, which optimizes their portfolio weights to maximize risk-adjusted returns. Empirical evaluations across seven major companies reveal that the multi-agent LLM + DDPG framework generally achieves higher cumulative returns than equal-weighted benchmarks and multi-agent PPO, though often with increased short-term risk. …
